description: Tokenized Asset Purchase: submit the custody arrangement for a purchased token: who holds the keys (the buyer, a custodian, the platform, the issuer or several parties); segregated or omnibus holding; the custodian with its name, regulator, license, status (active, suspended or revoked) and when the status was checked; how client assets stand if the custodian fails, whether bankruptcy remote and whether outside the custodian’s estate; the failure path with a successor custodian, the recovery process and the days to restore access; the latest attestation with its date, its author and whether it is independent; the custody wording, read for segregated, bankruptcy remote, your keys or self-custody; and the date custody is read at. The signed report gives the keys with whether a third party holds them and the wording found, the custodian with its regulator, license, status, the days since the status check and the attestation with its age, the segregation with the insolvency protection, and the failure path, and counts them, and names opaque custody: keys held by a third party with no custodian named, a custodian whose status is suspended or revoked, client assets inside the custodian’s estate, omnibus holding with no protection if the custodian fails and segregation, self-custody or bankruptcy wording the records contradict; then protected omnibus holding, an attestation over a year old or not independent, a status check over 90 days old and a recovery path with no time to restore access, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. Unstated keys, holding, custodian status, regulator, insolvency treatment, failure path, attestation and reading date leave custody unverified. This reads one token’s custody records: the custody and backing field the Atlas dataset records per issuer is wever_atlas-issuer-brief and one task passed between agents step by step is wever_chain-of-custody-check. Verdict tokenized_custody_opaque, tokenized_custody_partial, tokenized_custody_unverified or tokenized_custody_sound. POST /api/tokenized-custody-check. Reads the purchase records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Tokenized Asset Purchase reads the buyer’s own records for one purchase of a tokenized asset and checks each step before money moves: the quote against its stated terms, the platform’s terms against the buyer, the custody arrangement, the redemption path, the transfer restrictions, the settlement, the claimed backing and the full cost. Beside it, wever_atlas-asset-passport and wever_atlas-redemption-check read what the published Tokenization Atlas dataset records about an asset by its id, while a purchase check reads the records the buyer supplies for one purchase; and wever_vendor-quote-check and wever_price-truth-check read quotes and charges for goods, services and paid calls, while the quote and cost checks read a token purchase against its own terms. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/tokenized-purchase-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/tokenized-asset-purchase/.
